title: Enhancing Quality of Information Displayed on LCD Screens in MRT Trains
what_it_is: Enhancing Quality of Information Displayed on LCD Screens in MRT Trains

sections.label: MRT LCD screen wayfinding information
sections.summary: MRT trains have LCD screens above doors showing route maps, travel direction, stations and door opening side, with little feedback on clarity since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The various train models across different Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) lines are fitted with liquid crystal display (LCD) screens above the train doors, with some variation in the layout of information displayed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: They all provide similar information to help commuters in their wayfinding, such as the route map of the line, the direction of travel, current and upcoming stations, as well as the opening side of doors at the next station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Since 2023, feedback on the clarity of information on the LCD displays across the entire MRT network made up less than 1% of the total feedback received by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the operators, with no specific line receiving substantially more feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: LTA will continue to monitor public feedback and make further enhancements to our wayfinding features as appropriate.

sections.label: LCD screen design and rotating information
sections.summary: LCD screens vary by train make, with one-panel designs rotating information, and the North East Line does not show a commuter's approaching location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Depending on the make of the train and the design of the LCD screens – some come in two panels, some come in one panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, when it is the one-panel design, there will be rotating pieces of information that are displayed on the screen, but the frequency of display would suffice to allow commuters to read the information, interpret and react to the information within the space of travel between stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But if there are specific requests that the Member would like to make of LTA, I would be happy to follow up with him subsequently, so that we can look into enhancing the experience of all commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: I think the rotating information, sometimes you may miss out exactly where you are on the station and let us say you were not paying attention, for example, during the commute, you want to know in one look, where you are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: So, at the moment, I think, for instance, the North East Line does not exactly show a commuter where you are approaching.
